answer: In an agent economy trading terrace repairs, raven surveys, and walnut timber, voting power can depend on tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, with one token buying one unit of influence. Splitting 1,000 tokens among a thousand fake agents yields exactly the same total voting power as holding them in one account. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and forfeiting its use elsewhere.
